title: Jai Prakash Varma @ Rinku Singh v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Surya Prakash Kesarwani, J.; Jayant Banerji, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; Para 6.8 objection directed with stay of recovery.
headnote: A writ seeking to quash recovery of Rs. 7,08,521 by Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Limited was disposed of without any opinion on merits. The petitioner was given liberty to file an objection under Para 6.8 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 within four weeks; if filed, respondent no. 3 is to decide it in accordance with law within the next four weeks after hearing. Coercive action on the demand is stayed for eight weeks or until the objection is decided, whichever is earlier.
facts: The petitioner challenged recovery of Rs. 7,08,521 by Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Limited, Electricity Distribution Division-II, Varanasi. He sought certiorari to quash the Executive Engineer's 20 February 2021 request to the Tehsildar, Pindra, to recover that sum, and a 21 June 2019 recovery order of respondent no. 3 for the same amount. Counsel for the distribution licensee stated on instructions that the petitioner could file an objection to the demand, to be decided in a time-bound manner.

holding_units.topic: Para 6.8 objection as alternate remedy with stay of recovery
holding_units.holding: Without expressing any opinion on merits, the writ is disposed of with liberty to the petitioner to submit an objection under Para 6.8 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 before respondent no. 3 within four weeks. If submitted in time, the objection shall be decided in accordance with law within the next four weeks after reasonable opportunity of hearing. Coercive action on the impugned demand is stayed for eight weeks or till disposal of the objection, whichever is earlier.
holding_units.flag: Order cites Para 6.8 only, without a numbered sub-clause.

principle_tags.application: Court directed a time-bound Para 6.8 objection, reasoned disposal after hearing, and stay of coercive recovery pending that disposal.
Writ challenging the Rs. 7,08,521 demand was closed by relegating the consumer to the Para 6.8 objection, without a merits grant or refusal.

not_decided.point: Validity of the Rs. 7,08,521 recovery demand and the 21.06.2019 / 20.02.2021 recovery orders
not_decided.note: Court expressly declined to express any opinion on merits.
